data.name: Elite Warriors: Vietnam
data.detailed_description:
BEFORE THERE WAS DELTA FORCE, THERE WAS SOG

The Vietnam War’s most highly classified special operations were performed by the Studies and Observations Group. Consisting primarily of U.S. Army Special Forces “Green Berets,” SOG warriors fought top secret missions deep behind enemy lines.

Infiltrate deep into Laos with your Green Beret and Montgnard teammates, hunted by trackers and bloodhounds, outnumbered at times 100-to-1. Rescue downed pilots, ambush convoys, seize enemy prisoners, discover targets for air attacks, and direct air strikes. See why SOG veterans went on to found Delta Force and in the work of secret operations, remain the stuff of legends.

Features:

  • Take part in the top secret world of “Black Ops” unconventional warfare.
  • Engage in highly classified operation throughout southeast Asia.
  • Eight realistic campaigns that take place in multiple phases.
  • Use combat patrol techniques learned in Vietnam and still valid today.
  • Team building – train and equip your team and then lead them on covert missions.

reviews.review:
It's like the Oregon Trail, just with less cholera and more bullets.

This is such a fun game, even in 2026.  I'm currently starting my second playthrough of it after getting a new PC two months ago, and it still runs just fine.  Though I am aware some people have reported problems getting it to start.

The game puts you in the ranks of the legendary MAC-V SOG program.  Your selected team is tasked with performing sensitive operations like rescuing a downed pilot or recovering enemy code books.  Each team is comprised of two green berets from a sizeable pool (very reminiscent of Hidden and Dangerous 2) and two ARVN soldiers from a considerably smaller pool.  Loadouts are understandably small, but you have the option of directing the team to resupply points on the map.

Inserting, patrolling to the objective, and exfil points are done via a map phase in which random events can happen like a sprained ankle or clear terrain, reminding me of playing Oregon Trail.  Encounters with enemy patrols or making it to the objective brings you to an action phase where engagements are fought in third person, which is really what the game is all about.

Sneaking through the jungle is punctuated by chaotic firefights.  The environment looks good by comparison to the rest of the graphics.  The jungle really come to life in the audio however.  Hearing the bush rustle as your soldier pushes through it, the chirp of insects, and the rain slapping against the leaves is immersing.  Right up until it cuts out on you, a frequent occurrence which while not game breaking, can be frustrating.

The AI is lacking in many ways.  Enemy will run straight at you in waves while disregarding cover and friendly troops will often become stuck on a tree branch or a small pile of leaves.  When the AI works well, the game shines.  Enemies are lethal and know the jungle better than you do.  Which makes it so satisfying when you sneak up and dispatch one with your knife in close quarters.

The game was made with input from Vietnam veteran John Plaster.  Plaster served in SOG and wrote a book about the unit titled "SOG: The Secret Wars of America's Commandos in Vietnam," which is a great read that I also highly recommend.

Overall, I find this to be a genuinely enjoyable game.
